== Betrayal ==

The wiki currently states that Egwene's betrayer was confirmed as Beonin Marinye, citing chapter 24 of ''Knife of Dreams'' as proof. However, the relevant passages suggests that Beonin ''wasn't'' the one who betrayed Egwene:

: Beonin gestured and waited until her own Warder, a lean man with a long scar on his face, joined them. She adjusted her shawl several times. '''"Me, I betrayed nothing,"''' she said quietly. "I would not have sworn to you except that the Hall, it would have had me birched if it learned the secrets you knew. Perhaps more than once, even. Reason enough to swear, no? I never pretended to love you, yet '''I maintained that oath until you were captured."'''

To me, this strongly suggests that Beonin wasn't the one who betrayed Egwene. Betraying Egwene would be tantamount to Beonin breaking her oath of fealty, yet Beonin explicitly states that she "betrayed nothing" and "maintained that oath [of fealty] until [Egwene] was captured" - i.e. until ''after'' Egwene had been betrayed. Beonin is bound by the Oath Rod against lying, so she must be telling the truth: she did not betray Egwene.

Egwene herself believes this to be true:

: "I saw Beonin today," she said softly. "She's here in the Tower. She claimed her oath to me no longer held because I was no longer the Amyrlin Seat."

: Leane gasped and stepped near enough that she was brushing the iron bars. "''She'' betrayed us?"

: "She denies it, and I believe her," Egwene whispered.

Here Egwene states that she believes that Beonin did not betray her as Beonin ''was'' actually faithful to her oath of fealty until Egwene was captured. Beonin decided that Egwene was no longer Amyrlin once she had been captured and thus the oath of fealty to her as the Amyrlin Seat was no longer valid. 

Leane Sharif agrees with Egwene that Beonin couldn't have betrayed them:

: Leane glanced at the Whites. "Some always thought Elaida had spies among us. If Beonin was one, her oath to you would have held her until she could convince herself you were no longer Amyrlin."

It's my opinion that the identity of whoever betrayed Egwene is still unknown, and will probably remain so now the series is finished.

[[User:Nevtrev|Nevtrev]] ([[User talk:Nevtrev|talk]]) 12:59, May 9, 2013 (UTC)

== Spoilers ==

Has there been any discussion on spoiler-proofing entries for people new to the series because of the TV show? New fans will google Egwene after watching the show, only to have two major plot points spoiled for them!

People new to the series should not be exposed to so many major plot points on just the introduction of a character. The fact that she becomes Amyrlin seat is a major spoiler, the possibility of her becoming Aes Sedai is the first real hint we get of our villagers being special. The introduction of characters should give basic information about that character, info from the first introduction in the book and the first introduction in the TV series. Major plot points that are relevant to a characters biography can then be set aside in a dedicated section.

I've never been involved in a wiki before, so I have no idea how to implement it. I do want to learn to contribute, but this is something that I think needs to be addressed in less than a month, before the premier.

: Hi, this topic does occasionally come up. There is a peril in googling characters from an already existing IP on the internet and I don't believe there is much we can do about it. I attach a screenshot of the google search from my computer.[[File:2023-10-22.png|right|500px]] Any leading information is not viewable in the search, but what IS viewable is an image of Egwene with the Amyrlin's stole which isn't available on this website (Madeline Madden's face is in the artwork) and suggestions that Rand does not marry her and she is related to Gawyn Trakand in some way. The Google algorithm has the ability to extract information from the main text of webpages, so it's not really possible for us to make the wiki spoiler safe as far as Google is concerned. Also appreciate that this series was completed 10 years ago and started 30 years ago, so it's not really "new". Also, not all people care about spoilers. I did not when I read the series for the first time. If people do, however, it's an important lesson to learn to not Google characters from long-standing IPs and expect not to be spoiled. My main point, however, is that we have limited ability to control how Google displays it's information.  [[User:Moridin 2000|Moridin_2000]] ([[User talk:Moridin 2000|talk]]) 17:04, 22 October 2023 (UTC)
